scope: Incremental form and template fidelity; custom-element lifecycle remains excluded.
implemented: Option text/value fallback collapses ASCII whitespace while preserving non-ASCII spaces and explicit values.
Template contents share a lazy inert owner document per active document, including parsed/programmatic/nested templates, deep clones, import/adoption and contents moved into the active document.
Single/multiple select selectedness updates for default selected attributes, explicit setters/index/value clearing, size/multiple changes, option/optgroup insertion/removal and innerHTML replacement.
FormData fires a synchronous bubbling noncancelable formdata event with mutable entries and a recursive-construction guard; FormDataEvent and onformdata are exposed.
FormData includes dirname entries after successful text controls, with inherited/existing explicit direction and auto detection for common Hebrew/Arabic versus other letter text.

validation.jsdom_oracle: Tests compare option whitespace and ordinary dynamic select transitions with installed jsdom; template ownership also probed directly. jsdom selectedOptions stale-cache and duplicate-value select.value quirks are not copied.

performance_scope: No new per-node allocation in query/selectormatching paths. Inert template document is lazy. Template buffer content retains lazy node inflation; cross-document adoption materializes only adopted content and discards iframe lifetimes once per adopted subtree.
remaining_limits: No form-associated custom elements or ElementInternals.
File serialization consumes an existing files collection; a first-class FileList, native file chooser and complete upload-control lifecycle are not added.
Legacy object/plugin form controls are not emulated.
dir=auto uses first-letter classification for common Hebrew/Arabic text; this is not the full Unicode bidi algorithm or the complete HTML directionality algorithm.
This is ordinary select-state support, not every edge of modern customizable select content or every malformed-tree option ownership rule.
Native/full-Wistia integration validation is performed by the parent after all parallel runtime changes are integrated.
